certifications.name: HIPAA (Healthcare data privacy/security)
certifications.proof_quote: Nanox publishes a Notice of Privacy Practices Under HIPAA stating that, although it operates as a service provider rather than a covered entity under HIPAA, it has chosen to adopt HIPAA Rules in maintaining Protected Health Information (PHI); the Nanox Health IT page separately states "HIPAA-aligned security controls" and "Incident response planning & readiness." No public evidence found of a specific breach-notification timeline or of AWS infrastructure being independently HIPAA-certified.

flags: SEC filings (2025) note 'substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern' without additional funding, with an accumulated deficit of roughly $448.8M and a net loss of roughly $75M in 2025. This financial position affects vendor stability.

No public evidence of ISO 27001 or SOC 2 certification appears anywhere in Nanox's published Privacy Policy or other public disclosures; these terms do not appear in the documentation. Verify directly with the vendor before assuming either certification is held.

Unlike comparable enterprise healthcare SaaS vendors, Nanox does not maintain a centralized security or trust center page; compliance documentation is spread across its Privacy Policy, HIPAA Notice, and Health IT pages.

Nanox.AI trains on millions of anonymized medical images, and its AI-training stance is implicit rather than clearly documented: there is no explicit customer opt-out policy for AI training. Training does appear limited to anonymized data and internal/partnership datasets, not customer-specific patient data.

Nanox's role under HIPAA is ambiguous: it operates as a service provider (not a covered entity) and has elected to adopt the HIPAA Rules. Business Associate Agreement (BAA) availability is not explicitly stated in public documentation; a BAA is likely available but requires direct inquiry with the vendor.
